links.outcome: Expert-rated differential diagnosis quality of locally fine-tuned vs general LMs
links.effect: Fine-tuned LLaMa-7B beat LLaMa-65B (0.23 units, 95% CI 0.06-0.41, p=0.009) and BioGPT-Large (0.86 units, 95% CI 0.69-1.0, p<0.001).
links.quote: Fine-tuned LLaMa-7B performed better than LLaMa-65B (absolute difference 0.23 unit [95% CI, 0.06-0.41], p = 0.009) and BioGPT-Large (absolute difference 0.86 unit [95% CI, 0.69-1.0], p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Expert-rated quality of LM differential diagnoses compared with clinician-written ones on same notes
links.effect: Clinicians scored 3.43 vs 2.88 for fine-tuned LLaMa-7B, the best LM (difference 0.54, 95% CI 0.37-0.72, p<0.001). Clinicians ranked highest in 55% of cases, LLaMa-7B in 29%.
links.quote: The mean quality scores of the differential diagnoses generated by the clinicians and fine-tuned LLaMa-7B, the best-performing LM, were 3.43 and 2.88, respectively (absolute difference 0.54 units [95% CI, 0.37-0.72], p < 0.001).

screen.reason: Retrospective study where critical care experts evaluated the quality of differential diagnoses generated by general vs. domain-adapted LLMs compared to original clinician notes, with no specific organizational deployment safeguard tested.
